summary: Madhusudan Amilal Dhaky was a scholar of Indology, history, and archaeology who studied geology and chemistry at Fergusson College. He founded the Archeology Research Group in 1951 and served as Associate Director and Director Emeritus, Research, at the American Institute of Indian Studies.

Madhusudan Gupta studied at Sanskrit College and University and the Medical College and Hospital, Kolkata. Working in Indology and other fields, he taught Ayurveda at Sanskrit College (~1830–1835) and held a post at the Medical College and Hospital, Kolkata (~1835–1856).

Madhusudan Kaul Shastri worked in Indology and philosophy. He held posts at the Research and Archaeological Department, Jammu and Kashmir, serving as Director (attested 1918–1934) and later as Superintendent (attested 1943–1945).
Madhusudan Singh Vats was a scholar in the fields of history, archaeology, and Indology. He succeeded Rakhal Das Banerji (Rakhaldas Bandyopadhyay).

Maggie Bickford is a scholar of sinology, history, and archaeology who studied at Bennington College, Yale University, and Princeton University. She served as Professor of East Asian Studies at Brown University and was a Member of the Institute for Advanced Study (~1999–2000).

Maha Chakri Sirindhorn studied at Chitralada School, Chulalongkorn, Silpakorn (under Satyavrat Shastri), Srinakharinwirot, Asian Institute of Technology, and Peking University. Her academic work spans Indology, history, and archaeology.

Mahadev Govind Ranade studied at Elphinstone College, the University of Mumbai, and Government Law College, Mumbai, working across Indology, history, archaeology, and other fields. He founded the Maharashtra Girls Education Society in 1885.

Mahasi Sayadaw was a Buddhist studies and religious studies teacher who studied under Thelon Sayadaw, Aletawya Sayadaw, and U Nārada. He was Abbot at Mawlamyine Monastery (1941), taught at Mahasi Sasana Yeiktha, and founded the Insight Meditation Society (1979).
Mahesh A. Deokar works in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. He has served as Professor (attested 2011) and Head (attested 2020–2021) at Savitribai Phule Pune University.

Mahesh Chandra Nyayaratna Bhattacharyya was an Indology and philosophy scholar who studied under Edward Byles Cowell. He served as Principal of Sanskrit College and University (attested 1882, 1894, and 1914).

Mahinda Deegalle studied at the University of Peradeniya, Harvard, and the University of Chicago under Diana L. Eck, Frank E. Reynolds, and Wendy Doniger. A Buddhist studies and religious studies scholar, he held posts at McGill, Harvard, Colgate, and Bath Spa University.
Mahiro Ito is a Buddhist studies scholar who succeeded Norihiko Tanaka in 2021 and serves as a professor at Bukkyo University.
Maho Iuchi earned a PhD from Otani University (~2002–2008) and works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She served as a visiting researcher at Kobe City University of Foreign Studies (~2009–2011).
Mai Mishiro works in the fields of Indology and Buddhist studies. She held posts at the Japan Society for the Promotion of Science (attested 2011) and Waseda University (attested 2016).

Makio Takemura studied at the University of Tokyo and under Ryomin Akizuki, working in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He held professorships at Rissho, Mie, and Tsukuba universities, and served as president of Toyo University (2009–2020).

Makio Ueno is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed a PhD at Otani University in 2009. He held posts at Otani University as an assistant professor (attested 2010–2012) and was affiliated there in 2022.

Makoto Funaoka studied at Meiji University and worked in philosophy, Buddhist studies, and history. He served as a part-time lecturer at Komazawa University and the Open University of Japan, and became professor emeritus at Hokkai-Gakuen University (1993–2017).

Makoto Kitada completed doctoral studies at the Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg, working in Indology and linguistics. He held a post at the Nakamura Hajime Eastern Institute (attested 2008–2010).

Makoto Nagai earned a doctorate from the University of Tokyo and specialized in Buddhist studies and Indology. He held professorships at Toyo, Tokyo, Nihon, and Kamakura Women's universities, and served as president of Chuo Shoka Junior College (1951).
Makoto Yoshimura works in Buddhist studies and sinology. He completed doctoral studies at Waseda University (~1998–2003) and served as an assistant professor at Komazawa University (~2004).
